title: What happened at that exact moment?
summary: Synchronize commands, gyro motion, PID terms, motors, flight modes, craft attitude, and events on one timeline.
questions: What changed just before the wobble, dip, or disarm?
Did the command, gyro, PID output, or motors move first?
Which flight mode and craft state were active under the cursor?

blocks.text: A memorable half-second can look surprisingly polite when averaged across a whole flight. Graph keeps the chronology: command, response, controller output, motors, mode changes, and craft state can all be read against the same cursor.

steps: Choose Graph and add only the signals needed for the question.
Scrub or play to the event marker or visible disturbance.
Zoom around the interval and use range measurement when duration or spread matters.
Open the Craft section for attitude, motor output, flight mode, and reliable centre-of-gravity context at the shared cursor.

blocks.caption: A practical signal stack
rows: Whether measured rotation follows a pilot/controller request or appears without one.
Timing, saturation, and axis-specific response; availability depends on the log.
Did an actuator run out of room?
One or more outputs pinned near their usable boundary while correction is demanded.
Arming, disarming, mode transitions, and other decoded events in context.
Whether missing frames overlap the interval under investigation.

blocks.title: Order is evidence; cause needs corroboration
blocks.text: A motor output changing before gyro motion can support one hypothesis, but recorded output is a command, not proof of motor thrust. Likewise, an anomaly detector produces candidate intervals under specific eRPM and motor-output conditions; it does not inspect bearings, props, wiring, or ESC telemetry by magic.

When the graph reveals the right interval, switch to Table without changing the underlying time context. The table is slower to read but wonderfully literal: selected values and decoded events, row by row, with rather less interpretive jazz.
